item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed but slightly positive. By late 2024, Marcos had the Philippines on a somewhat stronger macro trajectory than in 2023: inflation fell, the labor market held up, fiscal numbers improved, and the IMF said the economy handled multiple external headwinds well. The caveat is important: the year started with a severe rice shock, and the main anti-inflation rice intervention had only partial pass-through and real costs for farmers, so this looks more like stabilization under constraint than a clean structural breakout.

**Accepted Claims**
- **IMF Executive Board Concludes 2024 Article IV Consultation with the Philippines** — International Monetary Fund, Dec. 19, 2024: [link](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/17/pr-24478-philippines-imf-concludes-2024-article-iv-consultation). IMF said the authorities handled multiple external headwinds well, growth stayed resilient, inflation fell to 3.2% on average in 2024, the current-account deficit narrowed, and gradual fiscal consolidation was underway. Best single source for “stronger trajectory than inherited,” though the improvement was helped by disinflation and lower commodity prices. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.

- **IMF Staff Completes 2024 Article IV Mission to the Philippines** — International Monetary Fund, Oct. 3, 2024: [link](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/10/03/pr-24355-philippines-imf-staff-concludes-visit). Midyear IMF staff said the economy had navigated multiple external headwinds well, growth was expected to reach 6.0% in 2024, inflation was expected to decline to 3.4%, and fiscal consolidation was underway. This supports the argument that the 2024 path was improving even before year-end. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`, `5B.6`.

- **Highlights of the 2024 Annual Average Inflation** — Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 annual report: [link](https://psa.gov.ph/price-indices/cpi-ir/node/1684065571). PSA reported annual average inflation of 3.2% in 2024 versus 6.0% in 2023, with food inflation easing to 4.5% from 8.0%. This is direct evidence that the price environment was materially better by year-end than when Marcos inherited the 2024 shock environment. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`.

- **Highlights of the April 2024 Labor Force Survey** — Philippine Statistics Authority, Jun. 6, 2024: [link](https://psa.gov.ph/content/unemployment-rate-april-2024-was-estimated-40-percent?vcode=2LnTw). Unemployment fell to 4.0% in April 2024, below April 2023 and January 2024, though underemployment remained elevated. This is a modest positive for trajectory: the labor market was not unraveling despite food-price stress. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`.

- **Philippines' budget surplus at P6.3 billion in October** — Reuters, Nov. 27, 2024: [link](https://interaksyon.philstar.com/business/2024/11/27/287793/philippines-budget-surplus-at-6-3-billion-in-october/). The government posted a monthly surplus and a smaller year-to-date deficit than a year earlier. That supports a finding of somewhat better fiscal control, though the deficit was still substantial. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`.

- **Philippine inflation quickens again in March as rice soars** — Reuters, Apr. 4, 2024: [link](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/philippine-inflation-quickens-again-in-march-as-rice-soars-3366872). March inflation re-accelerated, rice inflation hit a 15-year high, and the BSP stayed tight. This is the clearest counterweight: 2024 began with a severe food-price shock, so the year’s improvement was not immediate and came under real external pressure. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`, `5B.8`.

- **Rice tariff intervention had mixed results** — NEDA/GMA News Online, Dec. 10, 2024: [link](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/) and Department of Agriculture/PNA, Dec. 11, 2024: [link](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1239750) and [BusinessMirror](https://businessmirror.com.ph/2024/12/10/neda-lower-rice-tariffs-led-to-decline-in-farm-gate-price/). NEDA said the tariff cut did not lower retail rice prices as anticipated; the DA argued the cut probably prevented an even worse spike amid a weak peso and typhoons; NEDA also reported limited retail pass-through and a significant farm-gate price hit. This is the best evidence that the flagship stabilization tool had only partial success and visible tradeoffs. `5B.10`; also `5B.9`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`.

**Search Gap**
- I did not find any meaningful sanctions episode to evaluate for 2024.
- I did not find a clean standalone debt-series source in this bounded search; IMF fiscal-consolidation and current-account coverage is the best proxy.
- Overall read: stronger than 2023, but only modestly, and heavily influenced by external normalization, food-price easing, and public-spending support rather than a decisive structural leap.
